thread:
maya: heads-up — after yesterday's kernel-fallback tuning I see short-sequence p95 regressed ~30ms for seq_len < 32. kv-hit rate for those requests dropped ~6%.
ryan: ugh, saw alerts. is this batching related or kernel selection? any flame graphs?
sophia: do we have tenant breakdown? could be a few noisy long-tail tenants causing mixed batches.
maya: quick profiler dump below (sample from ci-run against canary nodes):
```
batch_mix: 58% mixed, 30% short-only, 12% long-only
p95(shorts): +30ms
kv_hit(shorts): 72% -> 66%
kernel_path: fallback->fastpath_switch more often for mixed batches
queue_wait_med: 6ms -> 12ms for short arrivals
```
arjun: hmm that points to batch formation/compactness. if the batcher compacts greedily to improve throughput it waits and pulls in longs, causing KV warmups and kernel affinity flips.
ryan: agreed. two knobs to consider: (1) "queue_compactness" target (how aggressive we are at coalescing different seq lengths), (2) hedged-prefetch window for short-only lanes.
sophia: propose simple experiment: bias mini-batches toward homogeneity by a compactness_threshold and allow short lane to spawn a hedged-prefetch after X ms instead of waiting. keep throughput SLOs safe.
maya: toy config i sketched:
```yaml
batcher:
  compactness_threshold: 0.65   # fraction of batch that must be same length class
  short_lane:
    max_hold_ms: 8              # wait for up to 8ms to gather shorts
    hedged_prefetch: true
    hedged_prefetch_ms: 3       # if not enough shorts, prefetch to fill token budget
  token_budget_strategy: by_percentile
  token_budget_percentile: 50   # use p50 sequence length to set per-tenant token_budget_target
kernel_selector:
  prefer_fastpath_for_short_pct: 0.75
  affinity_decay_ms: 40
```
ryan: i like `token_budget_strategy: by_percentile` — that avoids starving shorts on tenants with long-tail seqs. could we compute p50 at tenant-level rolling 5m window?
arjun: yes, rolling 5m p50 per tenant is cheap. then short_lane holds only kick in if tenant_p50 < some threshold, otherwise treat tenant as mixed and use less aggressive compacting.
sophia: telemetry we need: per-tenant p50, batch_compactness ratio, kernel_switch_count, kv_hit_by_seq_class. put these in the canary dashboard.
maya: i'll run a canary with compactness_threshold=0.7 and short max_hold_ms=8 on two racks for 1h. if p95 short drops and throughput stays within 1%, we roll.
deploy-bot: canary start triggered by @maya on cluster:canary-us-west-2 at 3887654330 :rocket:
ryan: also add a lightweight guard: if kv_hit drops > 4% for shorts during canary, auto-roll back the config.
sophia: i'll add the telemetry panels and an alert for kv_hit delta.
arjun: for longer term, we should consider kernel_affinity scoring in the selector so we avoid swapping kernels inside a batch when score delta < epsilon.
maya: agreed — short-term experiment first, long-term add affinity hysteresis and per-tenant token budgets.
ryan: owners: maya (canary + rollback clause), sophia (dashboards + alerts), arjun (selector change design). I'll help with metrics plumbing.
maya: thanks — will post a brief postmortem if we see regressions. :thumbsup:
